name: Pin Mux Explorer
blurb: a pin's alternate functions on an MCU and the conflicts
intro: Lists what a pin can do, which pins offer a function, and checks a full pin assignment: a pin used twice, a function on a pin that does not have it, F1 peripherals whose signals need different remap settings, and special pins (debug, boot, crystal). Data is transcribed from the chips' datasheets.

inputs.label: Pin to look up
inputs.placeholder: PA9, GPIO4, PD1 or a package pin number

inputs.label: Planned assignment
inputs.help: One row per signal; leave the function blank or write GPIO for a plain I/O.

examples.title: Blue Pill: UART, I2C and SPI1 on the remapped pins
RP2040: UART0, I2C1 and a PWM

usage: Give the chip (stm32f103c8, rp2040, atmega328p), optionally a pin name (PA9, GPIO4, PD1 or a package pin number) to list its functions, a function fragment (USART1, PWM3) to list the pins that offer it, and an assignment table of {signal, pin} rows using datasheet function names such as USART1_TX, I2C1_SDA, SPI0_SCK, PWM4_A, ADC0 or GPIO. It returns the tables, an issue count, the AFIO remap values each F1 peripheral needs, and warnings for double-used pins, missing functions, remap splits and shared-resource conflicts (F103 CAN + USB).
sources: ST DS5319 STM32F103x8/xB datasheet, table 5 pin definitions
ST RM0008 §9.3 alternate function I/O and debug configuration (AFIO_MAPR)
Raspberry Pi RP2040 datasheet §1.4.3 pin locations and §2.19.2 function select
Microchip ATmega328P datasheet §1.1 pinout and §14.3 alternate port functions
